tool.name: Refractometer
tool.measures: the refractive index of the stone, birefringence and optic sign
tool.where: Gemmology House and Office, top row, next to the loupe
tips: The drop of liquid first, the stone after
Turn the lens a full turn

steps.title: Refraction
steps.text: When light goes from one medium to another, it changes direction: this is refraction. Descartes' law: n₁ × sin θ₁ = n₂ × sin θ₂.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.text: Part of the light is reflected, at the same angle as the incoming ray.

steps.title: From high index to low index
steps.text: In the refractometer, light arrives through the glass (index 1.81) and meets the stone, which has a lower index. There is a critical angle.

steps.title: The critical angle
steps.text: Beyond the critical angle, all the light is sent back into the glass: this is total reflection.

steps.title: The shadow edge
steps.text: The border between the bright zone and the dark zone is the shadow edge: its position on the scale gives the index directly.

steps.title: The drop of liquid
steps.text: A drop of contact liquid fills the gap between the glass and the stone. The drop first, the stone after.

steps.title: One or two edges
steps.text: An isotropic stone has a single shadow edge; an anisotropic stone has two, which move when the lens is turned. The extreme values are noted: nα, nβ, nγ.
